summary: The text argues against tying E-Rate decisions to educational outcomes, extending CIPA to third-party-owned devices, requiring network-level content filtering, interpreting monitoring requirements and privacy, and changing CIPA's treatment of social media. It emphasizes the role of libraries in helping patrons, especially the homeless, find jobs and the importance of internet access for students who cannot afford internet service at home.

claims.argument: Third-party-owned devices should not be covered by CIPA
claims.evidence_quote: Libraries help patrons, especially the homeless, find jobs to help get them back on their feet, and internet/wifi access is the biggest help with that. Students go to public libraries to use their Wi-Fi to study or work on building a resume for a job at age 16 because their parents can't afford internet service at home. Public libraries help their community in so many ways and having internet access is one of them.
